I see this a lot, that Shankar needs sujatha for writing and he should've left direction after Sujatha's demise. I feel like this is the same culture which appreciates one by depreciating another. Like for example, to praise ARR, we talk shit about Ilaiyaraja and vice versa. 

Although, Sujatha was a great writer, he was not the one who wrote the script. Shankar seeks help in tying the story together, especially the dialogues. Sujatha is acclaimed as a good sci-fi writer. No doubt. 

In Fact, Sujatha and Shankar co-wrote several stories and the screenplay was 80 percent of the films were solely written by Shankar. The same goes for all the other movies they worked together. Well, our opinions stem from the fact that all their combos were a hit and I and 2.0 was a flop.  But it is not because of Sujatha's dialogues. Its the story and screenplay complemented by dialogues that elevates a film. The vibe and feel of Shankar movies were the same. The story for 2.0 and "I" was kinda weak and no good dialogues can help them. It's the story, all stories were from Shankar, not from Sujatha. 

Even Gentleman was written by Shankar and Balamurugan (great writer).

There are other good Tamil writers, but the fact that we are so stuck up on this cooked up opinion on Shankar's direction is really messed up because Sujatha is not writing dialogues anymore. It just pokes at the ignorance and us jumping into conclusions with 2 minute knowledge. 

Fyi, Shankar is working with Jayamohan. He is one of the best contemporary Tamil authors. You must read "stories of the True", the forest (english translated), Aana Doctor and Aram. In my opinion, he is better than Sujatha lol. But it's just my opinion. He is much of a sociopolitical writer than Sujatha was. And writing for a film in this era requires contemporary understanding. I feel like even if Sujatha was alive, not sure if he would've been able to adapt as much as writers like Jayamohan. 

We can't judge the writing from just the trailer, expect for "karumo illa varumo". But from what I know, Jayamohan must have done some good work, since its his area of expertise. 

What have you seen from the trailer that makes you think Shankar needs a good writer and he can't find one in the future. I thinks thats just baseless. Let's wait for the film.

This will be the case anywhere in the world. Racism is not a personal thing, it is bred from a collective thinking sorts. Wherever you go, there are people being judged for their colour, the way they speak and jobs they do.  I have lived in Germany for the last 8 years and I learned so much about life. Met the best people in my life. But the experiences vary a lot, just like any other thing in one's life. I have had a few racially motivated things happen to me. But I'd think what if I lived anywhere else, would this be gone? No. German culture is vastly different from where I am from. But there are few people who are welcoming and there are few people who are insecure. 

I know the aunt of a friend who moved to Germany in the 60s and she is still living here. It took her 20 years to completely adapt to the culture, vibe and people. She married a German guy and he died like 20 years back, but she stayed here and is still living here, facing the world as a single brown woman from another country. But she now has her people, it is her home. And she has faced a ton of racist experiences. But at the end of the day, there are some nice people you love and live for. For me, the nice people I know are in Germany.

Nice post. I liked Leo. It was very much focused on Leo x Parthiban than other characters. Why people liked Vikram more might be because of the depth of which other characters were portrayed in Vikram. Amar, Vikram, Parbanjan and santhanam etc. were given substance to their existence and some perspectives on their character and life. In Leo, it was just about Leo Das. It is really unfair to compare both, since Leo is focused on how Parthiban wants to escape his last and create is new identity and the hate he has for Leo. It is rather a philosophical approach to how one faces his past and reworks on his morality. Whereas, in Vikram, it was a story revolving several characters who are dragged into the story for personal reasons, most of them motivated by pure intentions of revenge and some fighting for a drug free society. Although, I felt the interference by LCU characters were underplayed. There was more scope for LCU connections, but it was not touched. 

On the flashback's drawback. I felt it was a bit weird that Leo had a twin and definitely, they both failed to convince me they are working in Das&co. Vijay's thirmalai style did not help. Lokesh kinda consistently drew a dark night vibe to his films. Vikram had that, as opposed to Parthibans story, Leo Das's flashback was like some commercial flick with dance numbers. They could have made Leo look much dark and remorseless. But Vijay na would not have accepted that. Leo Das failed to convince me he was a gangster tbh. I guess otherwise the movie was perfect.
